## Session Intent

This one's Ada's — she has to decide what to do about the courier before
the night is out.

## Session Overview

The party attends the Congress ball and Ada is cornered about Prague.

## GM Notes

Keeper only: Bram already suspects Ada recognises him from the delegation
staff list.

## Prior Prep Review

No prior plan existed for this chapter, so nothing was carried forward.

## Previously On...

Two weeks ago the party reached Vienna and took lodgings near the
Hofburg, and in the days since they have spent most of their time
learning the rhythms of a city that never quite stops watching itself.
Ada spotted a face from Prague among the delegation's kitchen staff on
their second night in the city, though she said nothing about it to
Winslow or Marlowe, choosing instead to keep the recognition to herself
while she worked out what it might mean and whether it was safe to act
on it at all. Winslow, meanwhile, spent his evenings cultivating a minor
clerk in the Congress secretariat, trading small favours and smaller
gossip until the man finally produced an invitation to tonight's ball,
proud of himself for managing it and entirely unaware of what it might
cost him later. Marlowe used the same stretch of time more carefully,
walking the Hofburg's service corridors under cover of a dozen invented
errands until she had a working map of every door the staff use and
never the guests, certain that a map like that would matter again before
the chapter was through, and hoping she would not need it under worse
circumstances than these. None of the three has told the others
everything they know, and that gap between them is quietly becoming its
own kind of problem, one that tonight's ball may or may not force into
the open before the night ends.

## Active Threads

The courier Ada recognised in Prague has not surfaced since the
delegation arrived in Vienna, and Winslow has quietly started asking
after him among the household staff without saying why he wants to know,
a habit that is starting to draw more attention than he realises. The
Brotherhood's promised letter of introduction, first mentioned three
sessions back, still has not arrived, and Marlowe is beginning to wonder
whether it was ever coming at all or whether tonight's ball is meant to
serve the same purpose without anyone having to admit it. Bram, who
works the Hofburg kitchens and has done for years, keeps turning up at
the edges of every conversation about the courier without ever being
asked into it directly, which nobody in the party has found a polite way
to mention out loud. The ledger he carries everywhere is the subject of
more rumour than anyone can confirm, and two separate delegation aides
have tried and failed to buy a look at it, for reasons neither of them
has been willing to explain, and the party still has no idea whether
either attempt succeeded in the end or simply went unreported.

**Location:** the docks — the last place anyone can place the missing
courier before he stopped answering letters from Prague altogether, and
a detail nobody has yet found a reason to follow up on despite how long
it has now been sitting untouched in the party's own notes.

No thread here has gone three full sessions without some kind of
attention yet, but several of them are close enough to that mark that
the GM should keep an eye on all of them going into tonight, especially
the courier thread, which has quietly outlasted every other lead the
party picked up since arriving in Vienna and shows no sign of resolving
itself without someone finally choosing to act on it directly.

## NPC Quick Reference

| NPC | Role This Session | Key Detail | Location |
|-----|-------------------|------------|----------|
| [[Bram|the broker]] | Runs messages for the Brotherhood | Never seen without his ledger | Hofburg kitchens |

Bram has worked the Hofburg kitchens for six years and knows every
servant's schedule better than the majordomo does, which is exactly why
nobody downstairs questions where he turns up.
His ledger reportedly contains names the Brotherhood would rather nobody
saw, and he has twice refused money to sell it, for reasons nobody has
been able to work out.
Whether that makes him trustworthy or merely patient is a question
nobody at the table has answered yet, and it may matter more once the
ball is properly underway.

## World State

It is the 9th of November, 1814, and the Congress recesses for the ball
tonight at the Hofburg, with guards doubled at every gate through Sunday
on the Emperor's own order. The Brotherhood publicly backs Metternich's
faction while quietly courting the Prussian delegation behind closed
doors, a split none of the investigators has confirmed outright, though
Marlowe suspects it from the seating chart alone. The faction posture among the smaller delegations remains genuinely unclear (apprentice guess — confirm), and nobody at the table has settled it definitively one way or the other, which is exactly the kind of gap this session should not be papering over quietly.

This plan revises the earlier draft that assumed the ball would be a single static location; it is now built around three connected spaces instead — the ballroom, the antechamber, and the kitchens — so that no single scene has to carry the whole evening on its own, and so that a PC who wanders off the expected path still has somewhere real to land rather than an empty room with nothing written for it.

No faction currently considers the party a threat, which is worth remembering before anyone gets tempted to push too hard tonight, and worth revisiting the moment that stops being true. The household staff are stretched thin by the ball's preparations and are unlikely to notice one more unfamiliar face moving through the service corridors before midnight, though that grace period will not last much past the first course being cleared, and anyone still wandering after that should expect to be challenged.

The weather has turned cold enough that most of the delegation carriages are queued along the Ringstrasse well before the first guests arrive, which gives Marlowe an unplanned excuse to loiter near the gates without drawing attention, and gives the whole party a longer window than usual to arrive fashionably late without anyone remarking on it. Candles are being rationed in the lower corridors to keep the ballroom itself blazing, which means the kitchens and the service stair are darker than they have any right to be for a night this important, and darker still than anyone downstairs seems willing to admit out loud.

## Planned Scenes

### Scene 1: The Kitchens

**Type:** dance
**Objective:** Bram tries to warn Ada about the missing courier without
saying so directly, in front of people who should not overhear it.
**Entities:** [[Bram]], [[Ada]], Hofburg Kitchens
**Setup:** Bram catches Ada near the servants' stair and asks after "an
old friend from Prague."
**Branching:** Ada can press him for the friend's name, brush him off,
or report the exchange to Winslow before the night is over.
**Complications:** A Brotherhood aide passes close enough to overhear
part of the exchange and lingers afterward.

> You feel a chill as the Spot Hidden reveals a shape in the corner.

The scene runs 45-60 minutes.

### Scene 2: The Ballroom Floor

**Type:** investigation
**Objective:** Winslow works Sternberg for anything he'll let slip about
the Brotherhood's real allegiance.
**Entities:** [[Sternberg]], [[Winslow]], Hofburg Ballroom
**Setup:** Winslow catches Sternberg between dances and offers to fetch
him a drink.
**Behaviours:** Sternberg deflects every direct question but drops small,
verifiable details when flattered.
**Branching:** Winslow can push harder, back off entirely, or bring
Marlowe in to corroborate what Sternberg says.
**Complications:** The guard rotation changes in 20 minutes, which the
party can use or lose depending on how the conversation goes.

The orchestra shifts into a new set, and half the room drifts toward the dance floor while the other half drifts toward the card tables instead. Sternberg keeps his back to the wall near the doors, watching the room rather than the dancers, and rarely lets a servant pass without a glance. A cluster of Prussian attaches trade quiet remarks near the punch table, switching to French whenever a Brotherhood aide passes within earshot. Somewhere behind the musicians a clock chimes the half hour, and a footman begins lighting a fresh round of candles along the far wall. Winslow keeps the conversation moving with practiced ease, letting silences stretch just long enough for Sternberg to fill them without noticing he has. A dropped fan near the refreshment table draws a small commotion, and for a moment three separate conversations pause to watch someone else's embarrassment. The ballroom doors open again to admit a fresh wave of guests, each announced by a steward whose pronunciation grows shakier as the night wears on. Somewhere near the terrace doors, two delegation wives compare notes on a scandal from the week before, neither aware how closely Marlowe is listening. A tray of empty glasses is cleared and replaced before anyone quite notices the exchange, the staff moving through the crowd like they are part of the furniture. The heat of the room is starting to show on some of the older guests, and a handful have already retreated toward the cooler antechamber for air. ## Contingency Scenes

### If Bram is confronted directly

**Trigger:** A PC asks Bram outright whether he knows the missing
courier.
**Type:** social
**Objective:** Bram has to decide, on the spot, how much to admit.
**Entities:** [[Bram]], the confronting PC
**Setup:** The PC catches Bram alone in the kitchen corridor and asks
him plainly.
**Behaviours:** Bram stalls for time rather than lie outright, hoping
someone else interrupts before he has to answer.
**Branching:** Bram can tell the truth, deflect with a half-truth, or
ask for something in return first.
**Complications:** A second kitchen hand walks in partway through and
Bram has to decide whether to keep talking in front of them.

## Session End Objectives

- Ada decides, one way or another, what to do about the courier.
- The party leaves the ball with at least one solid lead on Bram's
  ledger.
- At minimum, nobody blows their cover in front of the Brotherhood.

## PC Roster & Arcs

Ada is deciding whether to confront her own past tonight. Winslow is
working Sternberg for information. Marlowe is holding the map of the
service corridors in reserve for later.

## Open Questions

  Metternich.

Ada and Winslow split most of tonight's spotlight, with Marlowe held in
reserve for the corridors.
